Date October 29, 37.
Subject Public Works Department (Soochow Road) Depot - Agitation

Made by D.S.I. Laurier. Forwarded by C. Gimson

Reference the remarks of D.C. (Special Branch) on this
section's report of October 26 on the above subject: I have
to report that Coolies No's 102 Tsai Too Yung (蔡富荣), 282
Yuan Teh Soeh (袁德寿) and 429 Tsao Teh Ling (左德林) who,
as stated in the above mentioned report, formed a delegation
and interviewed Mr. T.K.Ho, Deputy Secretary of the Shanghai
Municipal Council, on 25 October, are not the real agitators
in the present unrest. However, the dismissal of these men
from P.W.D. service is at present under consideration by
reason of the fact that they disobeyed an order strictly
forbidding them to lodge complaints in person to officials in
the Administration Building.

The agitators principally responsible for the present
state of affairs have now been ascertained to be No's 143, 145,
188 and 206 (all Central and Northern). The P.W.D. Authorities
have been consulted regarding these agitators and state that
they are quite agreeable that these men should be placed
outside the barriers if this action should be decided upon by
the Police. In this connection Mr. Wellstead could assist
in identifying the offenders as he is able to recognize all
of them.

Subject Discontent amongst the unemployed workers of the Public Works
Department Soochow Road Depot.
Made by D.S.I. Laurier Forwarded by C. Crawford
With further reference to this sections report of
22 October on the above subject I have to correct certain
mistakes contained therein.
At the foot of the first page it was stated that
the Public Works Department had informed the coolies that as
from the commencement of last week they would be employed in
rotation, which would ensure each man's receiving one full day's
pay and five one-third day's pay per week which would be equal
to two and two-third days' pay per week per man. This is
incorrect, the announcement being to the effect that those
coolies for whom regular work could be found would be paid
normal wages as long as there was work to be done but that
should the present volume of work decrease at any time those
affected by the decrease would then be automatically placed
on the unemployed list. At the same time all unemployed
coolies attached to the depot, of whom there are some 1,800,
were told that there could be no guarantee of immediate future
employment and that so long as the Council were able they
would be paid, in the nature of a dispensation, an amount
equivalent to one-third of a day's pay per man. It was made
clear to them, however, that the Council was under no obligation
to either continue the dispensation indefinitely or guarantee
re-employment at any future date. This announcement by the
Public Works Department was made after the Department had
offer to repatriate and pay two weeks' pay per man to all
unemployed workers who desired to leave Shanghai. However
the 180 coolies who accepted these terms subsequently turned
the offer down necessitating cancellation of the arrangements
which the Council had made with the Shipping Company for

Subject Further to Disturbance over salary at the P.W.D. Markham Road
Depot.
Made by D.S.I. Taylor. Forwarded by O. A. Jenkins, Inspt.

Sir,
Since forwarding the previous report on this occurrence,
police have kept observation at the P.W.D. Markham Road Depot,
but to date no disturbance of any nature has eventuated.
Inspector Holt, P.W.D. has informed the undersigned to the
effect that there is now no signs of disagreement amongst
the coolies, as those entitled to various amounts of pay have
accepted same without further ado.
There is no reason to suppose, he states, that there will
be any further signs of disagreement amongst them and no

Made by D.S.I. Laurier    Forwarded by C. □□□□□

Mr. Brennan-Craddock of the Public Works Department gave
an interview to three representatives of the coolies in the
Soochow Road Depot at 10.45 a.m. on October 23 when the workers
were instructed as follows:-
1. The Council had now definitely cancelled its offer to
grant unemployed coolies two weeks pay and repatriation,
in view of the coolies' agitation for further extension
of these privileges.
2. The Council is definitely not prepared to continue half
pay benefits to unemployed coolies, though so long as it
is able to, it will pay them one third of a day's pay for
days on which they are unemployed.
The coolies' representatives reiterated continued payment
of half pay for unemployed workers and stated that they would send
a delegation to interview Mr. T.K. Ho if this request was not
complied with. Mr. Brennan-Craddock warned them that all members
of such a delegation would be dismissed instantly.
After further discussion Mr. Brennan-Craddock assured
the coolies that if they were prepared to submit a further
letter to the Council agreeing to dismissal on payment of two
weeks' pay that he would recommend, though not guarantee, ac-
ceptance by the Council.
The discussion terminated at 11.30 a.m. without further
incident.
The three representatives who attended are as follows:-

No.748 Zung Ah Yang 陳阿楊
No.102 Tsai Foo Yoong. 蔡富榮

Date 21st Oct., 19 37

Subject Disturbance over salary at the P.W.D. Markham Road Depot.

Made by D.S.I. Taylor. Forwarded by S. A. Perkins Insp. 110

Sir,
At 6.45 p.m. on 21/10/37, a telephone message was received from Inspector Hudson of the . . Dept., S.M.C., reporting a large number of coolies congregated outside the gates of the Markham Road P. . . Depot, causing a disturbance.

The Inspector i/c, C.I. Harvey, and a party immediately attended where it was found that 500 coolies, (150 on full-pay, and the remainder on part-time) were congregated at the above place, discussing the possibilities of the demanding of the reinstating of coolie No 39 who was dismissed by Mr. Hopkins, Assistant Engineer, about 14 days ago. It was also learned that it was intended to pay 150 of these coolies, but, these men refused to accept their pay unless the remainder were also paid, at the same time demanding that Coolie 39 be reinstated.

These coolies were finally dispersed, without any disturbance, by police, shortly after arrival.

Inspector Halt, P.W.D., will supply the names and other particulars of the instigators of this occurrence, in detail, when interviewed tomorrow A.M. 22/10/37.

Enquiries revealed that 350 of these coolies have been on half-pay since the 19th August 37, but for this weeks salary they were scheduled to receive 1/3 only, they being merely employed when work was available. This is partly responsible for the discontent.

No disturbance is expected, but observation is being maintained by police in the usual way.

A further report will be forwarded, after enquiries re the instigators of this occurrence have been made.

Enquiries proceeding.

At 9.30 a.m. October 22, upon receipt of a telephone message
from Louza Station, detectives attached to this branch proceeded
to the Public Works Department (Soochow Road) Depot. Upon
arrival it was found that a crowd of several hundred coolies
had collected in the compound and on the roadway and whilst
they showed no outward signs of intending violence it was
ascertained, upon entering, that the foreign staff, most of
whom had been there since 7 a.m. were unable to leave the
premises on account of the refusal of the workers to permit them
to do so. It was then ascertained that the present trouble
arises out of the present hostilities which have been the cause
of the closure of all Public Works Department Depots except
the Soochow Road Depot and the Gordon Road Depot. A large
number of those coolies who formerly worked in the depots now
closed were consequently taken on the strength of the Soochow
Road Depot and the regular staff of the depot, numbering some
700 men and the temporarily accommodated men numbering some
1,800 men were from 19th August, 1937, paid a full day's wage
for those days on which they were employed and half a day's
pay for those days on which there was no work for them to do.
Recently, however, the Public Works Department authorities
informed the coolies that as from the commencement of the
current week they would be employed in a rotation which would
ensure that each man received one day's full pay and 5 days
at one third pay per week, totalling 2 2/3rds. days' pay per week
per man. Strong objection was taken to this decision by the
workers, whereupon the Public Works Department authorities
offered, as a counter measure, repatriation and two weeks pay,
payable on board the boats at time of departure, to those men

To C. P. W., P. W. D.

We have been verbally informed by your officer that
our services are to be terminated owing to the curtailment of
road works during this period of emergency and that we are to
be supplied with passages to our homes.
We are much obliged to you for this kind assistance,
but we have to draw your attention to the fact that as we are
from different places, such as Shantung, Shansi, Chihli,
Anhui, etc., the evacuation of the whole lot of us together
with our families to Nantungchow, where we will still be miles
away from our native country, will not be the final settlement
of the case.
We, therefore, earnestly request that you will kindly
grant us all two months' pay to be applied to passages beyond
Nantungchow. As a souvenir of our service with the Council,
it is our sincere desire to retain our badges and we shall be
obliged if you can see your way to comply with this last
request of ours.
